questions.questionText: Why is a single embedding for an entire long document usually a poor retrieval unit?
options: Documents cannot be embedded at all
It blurs many different topics into one vector, making it a weak match for any specific query about just one of those topics
Long documents can only be embedded using RNNs
There's no real downside to embedding whole documents
questions.correctAnswer: It blurs many different topics into one vector, making it a weak match for any specific query about just one of those topics
questions.explanation: An embedding for a whole multi-topic document averages together many different subjects, diluting its relevance to any single specific query.

questions.questionText: What's the tradeoff between chunks that are too small versus too large?
options: There is no tradeoff, larger is always better
Too-small chunks lose surrounding context; too-large chunks dilute relevance and waste context window budget once retrieved
Chunk size only affects storage cost, never retrieval quality
Small chunks always retrieve better regardless of content
questions.correctAnswer: Too-small chunks lose surrounding context; too-large chunks dilute relevance and waste context window budget once retrieved
questions.explanation: Chunk size is a genuine design tradeoff — too small loses meaning-carrying context, too large hurts precision and burns context budget on irrelevant surrounding material.

questions.questionText: What advantage does structure-aware chunking (splitting at headings/paragraphs) have over fixed-size chunking?
options: It always produces exactly equal-sized chunks
It splits at natural content boundaries, keeping each chunk a coherent unit instead of arbitrarily slicing through sentences or code blocks
It's faster to compute than fixed-size chunking
It removes the need for embeddings
questions.correctAnswer: It splits at natural content boundaries, keeping each chunk a coherent unit instead of arbitrarily slicing through sentences or code blocks
questions.explanation: Structure-aware chunking respects the document's actual organization (headings, paragraphs), avoiding the arbitrary mid-sentence or mid-block cuts that fixed-size chunking can produce.
